newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Thousands flock to funeral of slain Sri Lanka MP.
newsitem.headline: Thousands flock to funeral of slain Sri Lanka MP.

text.p: Thousands of people in Sri Lanka's eastern Trincomalee city attended the funeral on Wednesday of a slain Tamil lawmaker, the latest victim of the island's long history of political assassinations.

Arunasalam Thangathurai, 61, a respected parliamentary deputy of the moderate Tamil United National Front (TULF), was killed in a grenade attack in Trincomalee last Saturday as he was boarding his jeep after inaugurating a new school building.
Four others, including the school principal, were killed and 15 people were wounded in the attack.
Leaders of various Sri Lankan political parties attended the funeral in Trincomalee, where security had been tightened to prevent possible attacks, police said.
Residents said hundreds of mourners including children had filed past Thangathurai's coffin, which was kept at his brother's house ahead of the funeral rites.
Police have blamed the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) separatists for Thangathurai's killing, but nobody has claimed responsibility for the attack.
Eight suspected LTTE rebels have been arrested in connection with the killing, police said. They had recovered Thangathurai's photographs and two hand grenades from one of the suspects, police said.
The LTTE are fighting a 13-year-old war for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east.
President Chandrika Kumaratunga said in a condolence message that the assassins had removed a leader who was dedicated to achieving a negotiated settlement to the country's ethnic crisis.

"It is abundantly clear that this dastardly act has been committed by frustrated and desperate persons to discourage right-minded persons from seeking a lasting peace in this country and plunging this land in anarchy and darkness," she said.
Thangathurai was the eighth TULF politician to be killed since the LTTE gunned down the party's former leader, Appapillai Amrithalingam, in 1989.
Several other Sri Lankan leaders have been assassinated in the past, including president Ranasinghe Premadasa in 1993 and presidential candidate Gamini Dissanayake a year later.
